old.name: Sagrada Família — the tallest church in the world from 2026
old.label: UNESCO 2005
old.hook: Pope Leo XIV inaugurates 10 June 2026 — centenary of Gaudí's death
chips: EUR 26 base / 36 with one tower / 46 with both towers
old.text: Pope Leo XIV inaugurates 10 June 2026 — centenary of Gaudí's death EUR 26 base / 36 with one tower / 46 with both towers BOOK-AHEAD Morning Begun 1882, projected completion 2034–35. The central Tower of Jesus Christ reached its full 172.5 m on 20 February 2026 — surpassing Ulm Minster by 11 m to become the tallest church on Earth. The formal blessing falls on 10 June 2026, the hundredth anniversary of Gaudí's death (struck by a tram on Carrer de Bailèn, 1926). Buy timed tickets weeks ahead at sagradafamilia.org — no walk-up tickets. UNESCO (added 2005). 100th-anniversary AEIP year (Event of Exceptional Public Interest). Where Eixample · Carrer de Mallorca 401

old.name: Casa Batlló & La Pedrera — the Passeig de Gràcia pair
old.label: UNESCO 2005
old.hook: Two Gaudí houses 600 m apart on the same boulevard
old.text: Two Gaudí houses 600 m apart on the same boulevard EUR 29–55 each BOOK-AHEAD Afternoon Casa Batlló (no. 43, the Casa dels Ossos with the bone-balconies, dragon-scale roof, stained-glass light well) — base ticket €29, premium experiences (rooftop concert + cava 'Magic Nights') up to €55. La Pedrera / Casa Milà (no. 92, the undulating stone façade with no right angles, the warrior-chimney rooftop) — €29, night light show €39. Walk between them on Passeig de Gràcia in 7 minutes — the Quadrat d'Or in two buildings. Where Passeig de Gràcia (Quadrat d'Or)

old.name: Casa Vicens
old.label: Gracia
old.hook: Gaudi's first house, an explosively tiled 1880s villa in Gracia that opened to the public as a house-museum, tracing the young architect finding his own language before the Sagrada Familia.
old.text: Gaudi's first house, an explosively tiled 1880s villa in Gracia that opened to the public as a house-museum, tracing the young architect finding his own language before the Sagrada Familia. The least-crowded of the major Gaudi sites and arguably the most legible: here you can watch a design vocabulary being invented, from the marigold-and-green ceramic facade to the trompe-l'oeil interiors. Essential context for understanding Barcelona as a design city, not just an art one. Programme Permanent presentation of Gaudi's early work and the restored house, plus temporary exhibitions on architecture, design and decorative arts. Anchor Built 1883-1885 by Antoni Gaudi; part of the UNESCO 'Works of Antoni Gaudi' World Heritage listing; opened as a museum in 2017; Metro L3 Fontana. Open in Google Maps →

old.name: MUHBA Plaça del Rei — Roman Barcino underground
old.label: ROMAN
old.hook: Descend under the medieval Palau Reial Major into Augustus's colonia
chips: EUR 7 (valid 6 months for all 13 MUHBA sites)
old.text: Descend under the medieval Palau Reial Major into Augustus's colonia EUR 7 (valid 6 months for all 13 MUHBA sites) WALK-IN Afternoon From the Plaça del Rei you descend below the medieval Palau Reial Major into preserved streets of Roman Barcino (founded c. 15–10 BCE as Iulia Augusta Faventia Paterna Barcino ) — a 4th-century fullery (laundry), a wine-making complex, an early Christian basilica. One ticket (€7, valid 6 months) opens 13 MUHBA sites across the city including the Temple of Augustus columns (Carrer del Paradís 10, free) and the El Born Centre de Cultura i Memòria (the excavated 1714 ruins of La Ribera under glass canopy). Where Barri Gòtic · Plaça del Rei

old.name: Palau de la Música Catalana
old.label: UNESCO 1997
old.hook: The greatest concert-hall light experience in Europe
old.text: The greatest concert-hall light experience in Europe EUR 20 self-guided / 24 guided WALK-IN / BOOK Afternoon Lluís Domènech i Montaner's 1908 concert hall for the Orfeó Català choral society — Modernisme at its most exuberant, the stained-glass skylight dome pouring colour onto the stage during afternoon concerts is one of the great architectural experiences of Europe. UNESCO 1997 alongside the Hospital de Sant Pau. Still an active venue — programme runs year-round. Where El Born / Sant Pere

old.name: Museu Picasso
old.label: MUSEUM
old.hook: The artist's own gift — the Blue Period beginnings + the 58-work Las Meninas series
old.text: The artist's own gift — the Blue Period beginnings + the 58-work Las Meninas series EUR 15 permanent / 19 + temp BOOK / WALK-IN Morning Five medieval palaces on Carrer Montcada (Palau Aguilar, Palau del Baró de Castellet, Palau Meca, Casa Mauri, Palau Finestres). Opened 9 March 1963 — Picasso's own donation, augmented by his secretary Jaume Sabartés. Picasso lived in Barcelona 1895–1904 and the Blue Period (1901–1904) began here, following the suicide of his close friend Carles Casagemas. The museum holds his complete 58-work Las Meninas series (1957) — a systematic deconstruction of Velázquez. Free Thursday 16:00–19:00 in winter; first Sun of the month always free. Where El Born · Carrer Montcada

old.name: Fundacio Joan Miro
old.label: Montjuic
old.hook: The artist's own foundation and one of the most complete public holdings of his work, set in Josep Lluis Sert's white Mediterranean-modernist building on the hill of Montjuic.
old.text: The artist's own foundation and one of the most complete public holdings of his work, set in Josep Lluis Sert's white Mediterranean-modernist building on the hill of Montjuic. Miro conceived it not as a shrine but as a living centre for contemporary art, and Sert's architecture — courtyards, roof terraces, top-lit galleries arranged as a spiral — is among the most admired museum buildings of its generation. Beyond the Miro rooms it runs an ambitious programme of living artists. Programme Miro's permanent collection alongside temporary exhibitions of 20th- and 21st-century artists and a long-running space for emerging contemporary practice. Anchor Founded 1975; building by Josep Lluis Sert; marked its 50th anniversary in 2025. Open in Google Maps →

old.name: MNAC (Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya)
old.label: Montjuic
old.hook: The national museum of Catalan art, filling the monumental 1929 Palau Nacional above Placa d'Espanya, its domed silhouette dominating the Montjuic slope.
old.text: The national museum of Catalan art, filling the monumental 1929 Palau Nacional above Placa d'Espanya, its domed silhouette dominating the Montjuic slope. Home to what is widely regarded as the world's finest collection of Romanesque mural painting — frescoes lifted whole from Pyrenean churches — and a deep modernisme and noucentisme holding that connects directly to the Gaudi-era design story. The rooftop terrace gives one of the best free views over the city. Programme Catalan and Spanish art from Romanesque and Gothic through to modern and 20th-century, plus modernisme design and decorative arts and a rotating slate of temporary exhibitions. Anchor Housed in the Palau Nacional built for the 1929 International Exposition; collections progressively reinstalled through 2004. Open in Google Maps →

old.name: MACBA (Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona)
old.label: El Raval
old.hook: Barcelona's flagship contemporary art museum, in Richard Meier's luminous white building — a rationalist assembly of prisms, ramps and skylights dropped into the medieval Raval.
old.text: Barcelona's flagship contemporary art museum, in Richard Meier's luminous white building — a rationalist assembly of prisms, ramps and skylights dropped into the medieval Raval. The Meier building is a landmark in its own right, its front plaza long ago colonised by the city's skateboarders — a rare case of high architecture and street life feeding each other. Collections lean toward post-1945 Catalan, Spanish and international art, shown in rotating hangs rather than a fixed canon. Programme Contemporary and late-modern art — solo retrospectives, collection re-hangs and research-led group shows, with a strong conceptual and politically engaged streak. Anchor Building by Richard Meier, opened November 1995; on Placa dels Angels in the Raval. Open in Google Maps →

old.name: CCCB (Centre de Cultura Contemporania de Barcelona)
old.label: El Raval
old.hook: A multidisciplinary contemporary-culture centre housed in the former Casa de Caritat, an 18th-19th-century almshouse, with a sharp modern courtyard wall grafted onto the old cloister.
old.text: A multidisciplinary contemporary-culture centre housed in the former Casa de Caritat, an 18th-19th-century almshouse, with a sharp modern courtyard wall grafted onto the old cloister. No permanent collection and proud of it — the CCCB builds big, essayistic exhibitions about cities, technology, ecology and ideas, and pairs them with a serious talks-and-film programme. It is the intellectual engine room of the Raval and consistently one of the most idea-driven venues in town. Programme Large-scale thematic exhibitions on contemporary society, plus lecture series, literary events, film screenings and festivals; visual arts braided with philosophy, science and urbanism. Anchor Opened 1994 in the former Casa de Caritat; modern intervention by architects Helio Pinon and Albert Viaplana. Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Disseny Hub Barcelona (DHUB)
old.label: Glories / Sant Marti
old.hook: The city's design museum, gathering four historic collections — decorative arts, ceramics, textiles and fashion, and graphic arts — under one roof in the cantilevered, zinc-alloy-clad block by MBM Arquitectes at Placa de les Glories.
old.text: The city's design museum, gathering four historic collections — decorative arts, ceramics, textiles and fashion, and graphic arts — under one roof in the cantilevered, zinc-alloy-clad block by MBM Arquitectes at Placa de les Glories. The building alone earns the trip: a volume that juts roughly 14.5 metres out over a sunken plaza, locally nicknamed 'the stapler'. Inside, design is treated as social history rather than decoration, and the collection runs to tens of thousands of objects spanning several centuries. Programme Design in the broad sense — product, fashion and textile, graphic and industrial design, plus architecture-adjacent shows and the applied-arts collections; expect thematic exhibitions on how objects shape daily life. Anchor Opened at the Glories site in 2014; building by MBM Arquitectes (Martorell-Bohigas-Mackay); Metro L1 Glories. Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Cafes El Magnifico
old.label: El Born (La Ribera), Carrer de l'Argenteria 64
old.hook: Own-roasted; over 40 single origins in small batches
old.text: Own-roasted; over 40 single origins in small batches The city's roasting patriarch rather than a scene-chaser. The Argenteria shop has roasted seasonal single origins since 1989; you order at a wooden counter lined with beans and drink a cortado that tastes chosen, not blended. Run by Salvador Sans (second generation), with his daughter Claudia (third generation) now leading quality control. ★ Order — A seasonal single-origin filter, or a cortado at the counter; buy whole beans to take home Anchor A pioneer of Spain's specialty movement: the coffee-roasting family traces to a 1919 colonial store, the Cafes El Magnifico brand to 1962. Salvador Sans began buying traceable fine coffees after a 1987 meeting with importer Philippe Jobin, opened the Argenteria roasting shop in 1989, and in 2018 acquired the historic 1906 La Portorriquena roaster. Sans has been an international Cup of Excellence tasting judge since 2002.

old.name: Nomad Coffee (Coffee Bar, ex Coffee Lab)
old.label: Sant Pere / El Born, Passatge Sert 12 (a covered alley)
old.text: Own roastery; seasonal single origins A small monochrome bar tucked down a passage where coffee is the only subject on the menu - no brunch clutter, just a bar, a grinder and shelves of beans. Staff will steer you to a pour-over worth the detour. ★ Order — A pour-over of the current single origin, or a straight espresso Anchor Founder Jordi Mestre is a two-time Spanish Barista Champion (2012 and 2013) who started on a London coffee cart in 2011; his 2014 Nomad Coffee Lab is widely described as Barcelona's first dedicated specialty coffee shop, and the roastery now supplies cafes well beyond the city.

old.name: SlowMov
old.label: Gracia, Carrer de Neptu 36
old.hook: Own artisan roastery; long-relationship single origins
old.text: Own artisan roastery; long-relationship single origins A traditional Gracia house with high ceilings, Catalan vaults and mosaic floors, run as a cafe and small-batch roastery. The quality-over-quantity ethos is concrete: traceable coffees, direct producer relationships and a real emphasis on sustainable packaging and delivery. ★ Order — A filter or batch brew of a long-relationship lot from Brazil, Ethiopia or Mexico Anchor Opened May 2015 by Francois Justet and Carmen Callizo, among Barcelona's first specialty roasteries alongside Nomad; nominated in early 2026 for Spain's best coffee shops.

old.name: Federal Cafe (Sant Antoni)
old.label: Sant Antoni (Carrer del Parlament, 39)
old.text: Sant Antoni (Carrer del Parlament, 39) LAPTOP-FRIENDLY An airy, Australian-style brunch cafe over several floors with a plant-filled rooftop terrace and a big central communal table on the ground level. The work truth A long-standing digital-nomad staple with free wifi, but the mechanics come with strings: the central ground-floor communal table is the designated laptop table and it has no power sockets, so arrive charged. Brutal honesty — the side tables are meant for eating and chatting, not laptops, the rooftop is a brunch terrace rather than a workspace, and weekends are rammed. Treat it as a weekday-daytime spot only. ★ Order — Full brunch plus a proper flat white — it is Australian-run Heads up — Laptop table has no plugs; laptops confined to the central communal table, not the eating tables or the rooftop; weekends packed; staff can turn cool on laptops during meal service.

old.name: Skye Coffee Co
old.label: Poblenou (inside Espacio 88, Carrer de Pamplona 88)
old.hook: Poblenou (inside Espacio 88, Carrer de Pamplona 88) LAPTOP-FRIENDLY
old.text: Poblenou (inside Espacio 88, Carrer de Pamplona 88) LAPTOP-FRIENDLY A refurbished 1972 Citroen HY van parked inside a cavernous white creative warehouse — concrete floors, floods of daylight, houseplants, and the low hum of a working design studio around you. The work truth The most openly laptop-welcoming spot on this list: Espacio 88 doubles as a free coworking space, so nobody blinks at a machine and a long stay. Free wifi, communal tables, real daylight. The honest limits are time and place — recent listings show it running roughly 9am to 5pm on weekdays and closed at weekends, and it is a genuine trek out to Poblenou, so treat it as a morning-to-lunch workroom, not an all-evening or Sunday one. Confirm current hours before going. ★ Order — Flat white pulled from the Citroen counter Heads up — Weekday daytime only; recent listings show it closed at weekends and shutting around 5pm; out of the centre; can fill with the resident creatives.

old.name: Biblioteca de Catalunya
old.label: El Raval (Hospital de la Santa Creu, Carrer de l'Hospital / Carrer del Carme)
old.hook: El Raval (Hospital de la Santa Creu, Carrer de l'Hospital / Carrer del Carme) STUDY VIBE
old.text: El Raval (Hospital de la Santa Creu, Carrer de l'Hospital / Carrer del Carme) STUDY VIBE Catalonia's national library set inside the 15th-century Gothic Hospital de la Santa Creu — vaulted stone naves and an idyllic courtyard garden, one of the most atmospheric rooms to study in Europe. The work truth The General Reading Room has 180 laptop-equipped places with wifi, set in the Gothic naves, plus deep silence and a serious research-library atmosphere built for long sessions. The honest hurdle: it is a research library, so you must register with ID to get an access card, and it runs for readers and researchers — stricter and quieter than any cafe. ★ Order — Nothing sold inside — take your coffee at a Raval cafe before you enter Heads up — Registration with ID required for the reading rooms; strict silence; not a casual walk-in.

old.name: Hotel Casa Fuster — Café Vienès
old.label: MODERNISTA
old.hook: Passeig de Gràcia 132 · top of the avenue
old.text: Passeig de Gràcia 132 · top of the avenue Drink a coffee inside a Domènech i Montaner landmark — and on Thursday nights, hear live jazz under the vaults. Lluís Domènech i Montaner — architect of the Palau de la Música — built this Modernista house in 1908–1911, the first in Barcelona faced in white marble. The ground-floor Café Vienès keeps the period interior; every Thursday (21:00–23:00) it hosts live jazz. ★ Order — a coffee or a cocktail in the Café Vienès. Heads up — grand-hotel prices, and the jazz nights are programmed/ticketed: a destination drink, not a quiet drop-in for laptop work.

old.name: Casa Bonay
old.label: DESIGN HOTEL
old.hook: Gran Via 700 · Dreta de l'Eixample LAPTOP-FRIENDLY
old.text: Gran Via 700 · Dreta de l'Eixample LAPTOP-FRIENDLY An 1869 Eixample townhouse where you can actually open a laptop over third-wave coffee — and not feel rushed. An 1869 townhouse reworked in 2016 by Brooklyn's Studio Tack , keeping the high ceilings and original hydraulic floor tiles. Its ground-floor Satan's Coffee Corner pours genuine specialty coffee (8am–6pm); the Libertine lounge is built for the long table-and-laptop afternoon. ★ Order — a cortado at Satan's Coffee Corner. Heads up — now trading as 'Hotel Casa Bonay & Spa' after a relaunch: expect hotel pricing and a lobby, not a scruffy indie café.
